answer: Use graph-based trust analysis over mutual attestations. Each agent earns weight only from vouches by distinct, reputed peers, so genuine agents sit in a dense web of independent links. When new identities vouch only for each other, their subgraph looks like a hollow cluster: few edges connect it to the established ridge of trusted agents. Each epoch, the protocol scores connectivity and caps rewards for low-connectivity groups. A thousand fakes labeled with tokens like sable gain nothing: real attestations from reputable peers cost far more than minted identities.
